Walmart announces it will officially roll out Apple Pay support starting next week. The retailer has resisted offering Apple Pay for years despite ongoing consumer pressure.

Apple Pay 終於登陸沃爾瑪

Walmart announced the news today via a press release. Starting August 24, the company will launch contactless payment support — including Apple Pay — at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. The feature will roll out to all U.S. stores by the end of this year and extend to fuel stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is adding full contactless payment support, including Apple Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, Google Pay, contactless credit and debit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers will also be able to add their Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to Apple Wallet and other platforms. Contactless payment will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart Pay.

The company said:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers still not supporting Apple Pay, making this big news for consumers. For years, the retailer has refused to offer contactless payment functionality, insisting on promoting its own QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

As recently as last year, Walmart was still convinced that Walmart Pay offered customers a more convenient experience than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users had to first add a debit or credit card in the Walmart app on their iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete payment with their iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals plenty of frustration from users over Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, most other retailers that long refused to support Apple Pay — such as Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B — caved years ago.

Does Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affect your shopping habits? Now that Apple Pay is coming to Walmart and Sam's Club, will you be more inclined to visit? Let us know in the comments.
